liner.body_md:
## Setlist highlights

- **Seastones 1 - Track 1**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 1 - Track 2**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 1 - Track 3**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 1 - Track 4**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 1 - Track 5**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 1 - Track 6**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 2 - Track 1**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Seastones 2 - Track 2**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]

## The recordings

- **gd73-11-28.sbd-seastones.finney.968.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 39 songs; 272 min; rated 3.15/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Listener describes the audio as a total meltdown, urging users to turn off lights; Recording contains spacey feedback and experimental elements, resembling a bad science fiction movie [2][4]

## Around the show

- Tarot outtakes derive from the T.C. album Tarot Touch, incorporating themes from his musical [5]
- From Seastones to Dark Star, the performance feels like one long strange trip [8]
- Ned performed the entire concert off-stage while Phil handled the live quad mix [11]
- Big Steve shared a story about this show on his XM radio program [12]
- A man calls out for a woman named Gloria, prompting audience chuckles and her reluctance to leave [13]
- This performance is considered far inferior to the released Seastones album by the reviewer [6]
- Early Seastones performance cannot be compared to the record, which is precisely constructed [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-11-28.sbd-seastones.finney.968.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Phil Lesh mixed the tape, which features Jerry Garcia, Mickey Hart, and Ned Lagin; MOTB release 0153, dated 2010-08-03, features Jerry Garcia and Mickey Hart at Palace of Fine Arts; Four-disc set includes three sessions from 11/28/73 and one from 6/6/75, via D. Finney [1][4][10]
